subject: StreamlinePay: proposal for surge attenuation, short canary, and customer readout
messages:
From: Alex Young <alex@streamlinepay.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Singh <psingh@streamlinepay.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent p95 latency spikes impacting checkout

Hi Tessa —

We started seeing intermittent p95 spikes in checkout between 08:30-09:00 PDT this morning. Rough outline:
- p50 steady ~120ms, p95 jumped from ~280ms to 2.1s for a 10–15 minute window
- Affected endpoint: /v1/generate-checkout-recommendations, call IDs: c3f9a2 / c3f9b7 (sample attached in headers)
- No config changes on our side; traffic pattern looked normal.

This is impacting conversions for a subset of traffic. Can someone from your side confirm whether there were runtime topology changes, a routing policy flip, or a kernel rollout around 08:00 PDT? We can carve out a low-traffic window if you need to run a canary, but were sensitive to any changes that affect latency.

Thanks —
Alex Young
Head of Platform Reliability
StreamlinePay

[attachment: sample-req-headers.log]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Young <alex@streamlinepay.com>, Priya Singh <psingh@streamlinepay.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p95 latency spikes impacting checkout

Thanks Alex — Im on it. Quick internal plan below, aiming for both immediate mitigation and a short canary so we can validate fixes without broad rollout.

Immediate ask (SRE):
- Ben: please enable a short protective rate-limit / circuit-breaker on StreamlinePay route to cap concurrent gen requests at +20% of baseline, with a 5m rolling window. Well remove if we see no regression.
- Soojin: prepare canary in us-west-2 to run a 2-hour window on a small traffic slice (2–5%). Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tail tokens, and kernel queue depth.

Product asks (Karthik/Marissa):
- Confirm whether switching to the smaller model variant (gpt-small-quant) is safe for StreamlinePay workload (quality regression risk and rollback steps).
- If variant switch is permissible, can we automate a quick fallback policy so customer traffic can be routed back automatically if error rate or p99 latency exceeds threshold?

Customer-facing note: Alex/Priya, well propose a 2-hour canary tonight at 22:00 PDT (your low-traffic window) and will provide a short readout after. If you prefer earlier, suggest a window and well try to accommodate.

I attached an initial incident summary for the internal bridge. Ill consolidate comms once we have a mitigation plan.

— Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
[t: +1 415-555-0123]

[attachment: initial-incident-summary.txt]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Alex Young <alex@streamlinepay.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p95 latency spikes impacting checkout

On it — quick technical plan:

1) Protective rate-limiter (short term)
- Deploy config to edge routing to cap concurrent gen calls per-token at 20% over baseline with a 5-minute smoothing window. This will shed excess concurrency and avoid queue amplification.
- Rollback path: remove config; we can apply at route-level and revert in <3m.

2) Model-fallback option (safe fallback)
- Stand up a gpt-small-quant instance pool as an immediate fallback. Quality delta should be small for recommendation scoring, but well flag outputs for manual review.
- Route failover: route-based fallback with thresholds on 5xx/error-rate and p99 latency.

3) Canary plan (coord with Soojin)
- I will provide a quick limiter patch (attached). Canary instrumentation will export: latency by kernel, queue depth, token throughput. Need a 2-hour run to capture a couple of traffic patterns.

Risks: we may see short-lived quality deviations on edge cases; customers should be warned about this in the briefing.

— Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

[attachment: protective-rate-limiter-config.patch]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Intermittent p95 latency spikes impacting checkout

Thanks — two quick product/roadmap clarifications:

- Model variant: switching to gpt-small-quant is safe as a short-term protective move for ranking/recommendations. Well mark outputs for quality sampling. No infra migration required, but the rollout API needs a canary toggle (we already have a flagged path).
- Automation: we have an auto-fallback feature, but current thresholding lives in SRE configs. Ben, can you confirm thresholds you plan to use (p99 > 1.2s OR 5xx > 0.5%)? If so, product can attach a safe-runbook to automate the fallback and auto-notify the customer.

Marissa: if were sampling outputs for quality, can your team prepare a quick prompt/eval checklist so the CS readout has objective signal?

— Karthik Iyer
VP Product, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Re: Intermittent p95 latency impacting checkout

Plan and ETA from infra side:

- I will coordinate the canary run in us-west-2 tonight at 22:00 PDT (confirmed with on-call). Canary config: 2% traffic, 2 hours, monitor p50/p95/p99, kernel queue depth, and token throughput.
- Ill push the canary runbook and a small script to tag requests with STREAMLINEPAY-CANARY header so we can filter in telemetry.
- If p99 exceeds 1.2s OR 5xx > 0.5% during the run, well auto-fallback to gpt-small-quant and cut the canary.

Im attaching the canary runbook and the test script. I can run a dry-run in the next hour in staging if anyone wants to validate the metrics pipeline.

— Soojin Lee
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Platform

[attachment: canary-runbook.md]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Young <alex@streamlinepay.com>, Priya Singh <psingh@streamlinepay.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: StreamlinePay: planned mitigation & proposed canary tonight (customer readout)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thank you for the quick signal this morning. Below is the short readout and our proposed next steps. Well keep this brief so you can share with stakeholders.

Summary of what we observed:
- Short p95 spikes in the checkout recommendation endpoint between ~08:30–09:00 PDT on 2027-04-19.
- No config changes on your side reported; telemetry suggests transient queue amplification on a subset of inference kernels.

Immediate mitigations (already prepared):
- Protective rate-limiter deployed at edge routing (config can be reverted quickly). This reduces queue amplification and shortens tail latency risk.
- Standby fallback to gpt-small-quant (lower memory, faster kernels) prepared — this will only be used if p99 > 1.2s OR 5xx > 0.5%.

Proposed canary (requesting your sign-off):
- Window: Tonight, 22:00–00:00 PDT (we picked this as your low-traffic window; confirm if you prefer another).
- Scope: 2% of traffic routed to the canary variant in us-west-2.
- Success metrics: p95 <= 400ms and p99 <= 1.2s, 5xx < 0.5%.

What we need from you:
- Confirm the 22:00 PDT window or propose an alternative.
- If you want, we can run a dry staging canary earlier and share the logs.

Well send a short post-canary readout within 45 minutes of completion. If we see regressions during the canary, well auto-fallback and notify you immediately.

Thanks — and apologies for the disruption. Were prioritizing minimizing customer experience impact and will follow up with the post-run results.

— Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
